facts.statement: Einiosaurus lived during the Upper Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Upper Cretaceous,

facts.statement: Einiosaurus was a herbivorous centrosaurine ceratopsian dinosaur that lived in northwestern Montana during the Campanian stage of the Upper Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Einiosaurus is a genus of herbivorous centrosaurine ceratopsian dinosaur from the Upper Cretaceous (Campanian stage) of northwestern Montana.

facts.statement: Einiosaurus was a medium-sized dinosaur with an estimated body length of 4.5 meters.
facts.quote: Einiosaurus is medium-sized with an estimated body length at 4.5 m.

facts.statement: Remains of at least fifteen individuals of varying ages, including three adult skulls, were discovered by Jack Horner in 1985 and excavated between 1985 and 1989.
facts.quote: At least fifteen individuals of varying ages are represented by three adult skulls and hundreds of other bones from two low-diversity, monospecific (one species) bonebeds, which were discovered by Jack Horner in 1985 and excavated from 1985 to 1989 by Museum of the Rockies field crews.

facts.statement: In late August 1986, Horner and Carrie Ancell discovered the Canyon Bone Bed, a site containing two relatively complete skulls located one mile from the first quarry.
facts.quote: In late August 1986, Horner and preparator Carrie Ancell on the land of Gloria Sundquist discovered a second horned dinosaur site, at one mile distance from the first, called the Canyon Bone Bed, in which two relatively complete skulls were dug up.

facts.statement: The two skulls found at the Canyon Bone Bed weighed approximately half a tonne when plastered and had to be airlifted from a steep cliff.
facts.quote: The skulls had to be removed from a rather steep cliff and weighed about half a tonne when plastered.

facts.statement: Expeditions ended in 1990 after commercial fossil hunters used bulldozers to strip-min the sites, diminishing the scientific value of the discoveries.
facts.quote: In 1990, the expeditions were ended because the reservation allowed access to commercial fossil hunters who quickly strip-mined sites with bulldozers, through a lack of proper documentation greatly diminishing the scientific value of the discoveries.

facts.statement: All known remains of Einiosaurus are housed at the Museum of the Rockies in Bozeman, Montana.
facts.quote: All of its known remains are currently held at the Museum of the Rockies in Bozeman, Montana.

facts.statement: The specific name procurvicornis refers to the forward-curving nasal horn of the dinosaur.
facts.quote: The specific name is derived from Latin procurvus, "bent forwards", and cornu, "horn", referring to the forwards curving nasal horn.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was found in the Two Medicine Formation, which dates to the late Campanian stage.
facts.quote: The holotype, MOR 456-8-9-6-1, was found in a layer of the Two Medicine Formation dating from the late Campanian.

facts.statement: Sampson named the genus and species Einiosaurus procurvicornis in 1994 based on Horner's "Taxon B".
facts.quote: In 1994, Sampson, in a talk during the annual meeting of the Society of Vertebrate Paleontology, named Horner's "Taxon B" as a new genus and species, Einiosaurus procurvicornis.

facts.statement: The generic name Einiosaurus combines the Blackfeet word for 'American bison' and the Greek word for 'lizard'.
facts.quote: The generic name Einiosaurus is derived from the Blackfeet eini, "American bison", and Latinised Greek saurus, "lizard".

facts.statement: Sampson chose the name to honor the Blackfeet tribe and to reflect the herd-living nature of ceratopsids, which he called 'the buffalo of the Cretaceous'.
facts.quote: The name was chosen to honour the Blackfeet tribe but also to reflect the fact that ceratopsids were, in Sampson's words, "the buffalo of the Cretaceous", living in herds and having a complex life.

facts.statement: Peter Dodson argued in 1990 that the fossil material supported the validity of Styracosaurus ovatus as a distinct species from Styracosaurus albertensis.
facts.quote: In 1990, the fossil material was seen by Dodson as strengthening the case for the validity of a separate Styracosaurus ovatus, to be distinguished from Styracosaurus albertensis.

facts.statement: In 1992, Horner described the fossils as three unnamed transitional taxa bridging the gap between Styracosaurus and Pachyrhinosaurus.
facts.quote: In 1992, he described them in an article as three "transitional taxa" that had spanned the gap between the older Styracosaurus and the later Pachyrhinosaurus. He deliberately declined to name these three taxa.

facts.statement: In 2006, researchers proposed that the dubious species Monoclonius lowei might actually be a sub-adult specimen of Einiosaurus.
facts.quote: In 2006, it was also proposed that Monoclonius lowei, a dubious species based on a skull (specimen CMN 8790) from the Dinosaur Park Formation, could be a sub-adult specimen of Styracosaurus, Einiosaurus, or Achelousaurus

facts.statement: In 2021, John Wilson and Jack Scannella suggested that the subadult specimen MOR 591, previously assigned to Achelousaurus, could possibly belong to Einiosaurus.
facts.quote: The subadult specimen MOR 591 from the uppermost Two Medicine Formation was assigned to Achelousaurus in 1995 and henceforward, but in 2021, John Wilson and Jack Scannella stated that it could also possibly belong to Einiosaurus

facts.statement: Einiosaurus was a herbivorous dinosaur that was generally as large as Achelousaurus but far less robust.
facts.quote: Einiosaurus was a herbivorous dinosaur. It is generally as large as Achelousaurus, though far less robust.

facts.statement: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated the body length of Einiosaurus at 4.5 meters and its weight at 1.3 tonnes.
facts.quote: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated the body length of Einiosaurus at 4.5 m, its weight at 1.3 t.

facts.statement: The supraorbital "brow" horns of Einiosaurus are low, rounded, and have a convex surface on the inner side.
facts.quote: The supraorbital "brow" horns as far as they are present are low and rounded with a convex surface on the inner side.

facts.statement: Six adult nasal horn cores were found, showing two types: two were small and erect, while four were large and strongly curved to the front.
facts.quote: Six cores were of adults. They showed two distinctive types. Two cores were small and erect, i.e. vertically directed. The four others were large and procurved, strongly curving to the front.

facts.statement: According to Sampson, the replacement of brow horns with pits or masses reflects a general trend in centrosaurines to re-absorb these horns in later life.
facts.quote: According to Sampson, this reflects a general trend with centrosaurines to re-absorb the brow horns in later life.

facts.statement: In Einiosaurus, the supracranial cavity runs sideways and continues down into the brow horn.
facts.quote: In Einiosaurus, this cavity runs sideways, continuing to below into the brow horn.

facts.statement: Smaller osteoderms adorn the frill edge of Einiosaurus, while the first epiparietals are largely absent.
facts.quote: Smaller osteoderms adorn the frill edge. The first epiparietals are largely absent.

facts.statement: The species originally labeled as "Transitional Taxon B" by Horner was later formally named Einiosaurus.
facts.quote: Subsequently, "Taxon A" was named Stellasaurus, "Taxon B" became Einiosaurus, while "Taxon C" became Achelousaurus.

facts.statement: Einiosaurus lived on a narrow coastal strip in Laramidia, bordered by the Western Interior Seaway and the 3 to 4 km high proto-Rocky Mountains.
facts.quote: The animals were living on a narrow strip on the east-coast of Laramidia, bordering the Western Interior Seaway and constrained in the west by the 3 to 4 km high proto-Rocky Mountains.

facts.statement: Horner hypothesized that Einiosaurus represented a transitional form in an anagenetic lineage, arguing that the species evolved gradually without splitting into separate branches.
facts.quote: Horner noted that the newer forms often had a strong similarity to the previous types. This suggested to him that he had discovered a rare proof of evolution in action: the later fauna was basically the old one but at a more evolved stage.

facts.statement: Some researchers, such as Dodson, argued against the anagenesis hypothesis, suggesting that the single pair of spikes in Einiosaurus indicated it was a separate branch rather than a direct descendant of Styracosaurus.
facts.quote: In 1996, Dodson raised two objections to Horner's hypothesis. Firstly, the possession of just one pair of main spikes seemed more basal than the presence of three pairs, as with Styracosaurus albertensis.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the differences between Einiosaurus and Achelousaurus represent distinct species evolving over time or sexual dimorphism within a single species.
facts.quote: Secondly, he was concerned that Einiosaurus and Achelousaurus were a case of sexual dimorphism, one type being the males, the other the females.

facts.statement: Later studies by Wilson and Scannella supported the idea that Achelousaurus was the direct descendant of Einiosaurus, with adult Einiosaurus showing morphology similar to Achelousaurus.
facts.quote: They concluded that Achelousaurus was likely the direct descendant of Einiosaurus. The more adult Einiosaurus individuals approached the Achelousaurus morphology.

facts.statement: Einiosaurus is classified within the family Ceratopsidae, specifically in the subfamily Centrosaurinae.
facts.quote: In 1995, Sampson formally placed Einiosaurus in the Ceratopsidae, more precisely the Centrosaurinae.

facts.statement: Einiosaurus belongs to the clade Pachyrhinosaurini, which also includes Achelousaurus.
facts.quote: In all analyses, Einiosaurus and Achelousaurus are part of the clade Pachyrhinosaurini.

facts.statement: While Gregory S. Paul once assigned Einiosaurus to the genus Centrosaurus, this classification has not been accepted by other researchers who continue to use the name Einiosaurus.
facts.quote: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul assigned E. procurvicornis to the genus Centrosaurus, as C. procurvicornis. This has found no acceptance among other researchers, with subsequent taxonomic assessments invariably keeping the generic name Einiosaurus.

facts.statement: Scientists have debated whether Styracosaurus albertensis or Einiosaurus was the direct ancestor of Achelousaurus, with studies yielding conflicting results.
facts.quote: Subsequent studies have sought to determine the precise relationships within this part of the evolutionary tree, with conflicting results regarding the question whether Styracosaurus albertensis or Einiosaurus might have been in the direct line of ascent to Achelousaurus.

facts.statement: Einiosaurus possessed a complex dental battery that allowed it to process tough vegetation.
facts.quote: Like all ceratopsids, Einiosaurus had a complex dental battery capable of processing even the toughest plants.

facts.statement: Einiosaurus inhabited inland environments.
facts.quote: Einiosaurus lived in an inland habitat.

facts.statement: In 1995, Sampson argued against sexual dimorphism between Einiosaurus and Achelousaurus based on bone bed evidence, age differences, and the nature of secondary sexual characters.
facts.quote: Sampson in 1995 rejected the possibility that the difference in skull ornamentation between Einiosaurus and Achelousaurus represented sexual dimorphism, for three reasons.

facts.statement: Single-species bone beds of Einiosaurus are interpreted as evidence of herding behavior, possibly resulting from catastrophic events like droughts or floods.
facts.quote: Low-diversity and single-species bonebeds are thought to represent herds that may have died in catastrophic events, such as during a drought or flood.

facts.statement: Einiosaurus is considered a herding animal with behavior similar to modern bison or wildebeest.
facts.quote: This is evidence that Einiosaurus, as well as other centrosaurine ceratopsians such as Pachyrhinosaurus and Centrosaurus, were herding animals similar in behavior to modern-day bison or wildebeest.

facts.statement: Oxygen isotope analysis suggests Einiosaurus was a homeothermic endotherm, maintaining a constant body temperature.
facts.quote: The variation of the dinosaurs, including MOR 591, was consistent with them being homeothermic endotherms.

facts.statement: A 2010 study concluded that Einiosaurus experienced rapid growth until its third to fifth year, likely coinciding with sexual maturity.
facts.quote: In 2010, a study by Julie Reizner of the individuals excavated at the Dino Ridge site concluded that Einiosaurus grew quickly until its third to fifth year of life after which growth slowed, probably at the onset of sexual maturity.

facts.statement: A 2021 study noted a discrepancy where a younger specimen of similar size to an adult Einiosaurus skull exists, raising questions about growth rates if the younger specimen belongs to Achelousaurus.
facts.quote: In 2021 a study, Wilson and Scannella pointed out that specimen MOR 591 was of a younger individual age than the Einiosaurus skull MOR 456 8-8-87-1, but of the same size.

facts.statement: Einiosaurus lived between 83 and 74 million years ago during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous Period.
facts.quote: Einiosaurus is known from the Two Medicine Formation, which preserves coastal sediments dating from the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous Period, between 83 and 74 million years ago.

facts.statement: Einiosaurus lived in what is now North America.
facts.quote: en lo que hoy es Norteamérica

facts.statement: Einiosaurus lived in a warm semiarid climate.
facts.quote: The Two Medicine Formation is typified by a warm semiarid climate.

facts.statement: A 2013 study determined that Einiosaurus was restricted to feeding on vegetation 1 meter or lower in height.
facts.quote: Einiosaurus ate much smaller plants, though: a 2013 study determined that ceratopsid herbivores on Laramidia were restricted to feeding on vegetation with a height of 1 m or lower.

facts.statement: Einiosaurus was a herbivorous dinosaur.
facts.quote: Einiosaurus era un dinosaurio herbívoro.

facts.statement: Einiosaurus possessed a distinctive nasal horn that curved downward and forward.
facts.quote: Einiosaurus presentaba un característico cuerno nasal curvado hacia abajo y adelante.

facts.quote: Los cuernos supraorbitales son bajos y redondeados, a diferencia de los prominentes cuernos supraorbitales de ceratópsidos como los tricerátopos.

facts.statement: Two long spikes projected backward from the short frill of Einiosaurus.
facts.quote: Desde la gola, que era corta, se proyectan hacia atrás dos espinas largas.

facts.statement: Like all ceratopsids, Einiosaurus had a complex dental battery capable of processing even the toughest plants.
facts.quote: Einiosaurus era un dinosaurio herbívoro. Como todos los ceratópsidos, tenía una batería dental compleja capaz de procesar incluso las plantas más resistentes.

facts.statement: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated Einiosaurus to be 4.5 meters long and weigh 1.3 tonnes.
facts.quote: En 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimó la longitud de su cuerpo en 4,5metros y su peso en 1,3toneladas.

facts.statement: Einiosaurus had a narrow and very pointed snout.
facts.quote: Su hocico es estrecho y muy puntiagudo.

facts.statement: Einiosaurus usually had a low nasal horn curving strongly forward and downward like a bottle opener, though this feature only appears in some adults.
facts.quote: Por lo general, se presenta con un cuerno nasal bajo, fuertemente hacia adelante y hacia abajo que se parece a un abrebotellas, aunque esto solo puede ocurrir en algunos adultos.

facts.statement: The supraorbital horns above the eye were low, short, and triangular when viewed from above, if present.
facts.quote: Los cuernos supraorbitarios, sobre el ojo, son bajos, cortos y triangulares en vista superior, si están presentes

facts.statement: Einiosaurus had a pair of large spikes, the third parietal epiparietals, projecting backward from a relatively small frill.
facts.quote: Un par de espigas grandes, las terceras epiparietales, se proyectan hacia atrás desde un volante relativamente pequeño.

facts.statement: Smaller osteoderms adorned the edge of the frill.
facts.quote: Osteodermos más pequeños adornan el borde del volante.

facts.statement: The first epiparietals were largely absent in Einiosaurus.
facts.quote: Los primeros epiparietales están en gran parte ausentes.

facts.statement: Einiosaurus is found exclusively in Montana, USA, and all known specimens are housed at the Museum of the Rockies in Bozeman, Montana.
facts.quote: Einiosaurus es un dinosaurio exclusivamente de Montana, EE. UU., y todos sus restos conocidos se guardan actualmente en el Museo de las Rocosas en Bozeman, Montana.

facts.statement: The fossils were discovered by Jack Horner between 1985 and 1989.
facts.quote: que fueron descubiertos por Jack Horner entre 1985 y 1989

facts.statement: The holotype of Einiosaurus is MOR 456.
facts.quote: El holotipo de Einiosaurus es MOR 456.

facts.quote: El nombre genérico deriva del lenguaje de los nativos americanos Pies negros para el "bisonte" y del griego para "lagarto".

facts.statement: Einiosaurus belongs to the family Ceratopsidae.
facts.quote: familia: Ceratopsidae

facts.statement: The closest relatives of Einiosaurus are considered to be Centrosaurus and Styracosaurus, or Achelousaurus and Pachyrhinosaurus.
facts.quote: sus parientes más cercanos son Centrosaurus y Styracosaurus o Achelousaurus y Pachyrhinosaurus.

facts.statement: Horner et al. support the hypothesis that Einiosaurus is the earliest form in a transition series where nasal horns gradually change from rough lumps, as seen in Achelousaurus and Pachyrhinosaurus.
facts.quote: La última hipótesis es apoyada por Horner et al., donde coloca al Einiosaurus como la forma más temprana en una serie de transiciones en la cual los cuernos nasales cambian gradualmente de los bultos rugosos, como en Achelousaurus y Pachyrhinosaurus donde estos son los segundos y terceros en esta serie.

facts.statement: Tooth marks on horned dinosaur fossils suggest they were scavenged by a large theropod predator, possibly Albertosaurus.
facts.quote: As proven by tooth marks, horned dinosaur fossils in the Landslide Butte Field Area had been scavenged by a large theropod predator, which Rogers suggested were Albertosaurus.

facts.statement: It is uncertain exactly which fauna Einiosaurus shared a habitat with, as its fossils have not been found in direct association with other taxa.
facts.quote: The exact composition of the fauna Einiosaurus was part of is uncertain, as its fossils have not been discovered in direct association with other taxa.

facts.statement: While Horner assumed Einiosaurus and Achelousaurus were separate in time, Henderson suggested in 2010 that their ancestors or descendants might have overlapped and competed for food unless niche partitioning occurred.
facts.quote: Whereas Horner assumed that Einiosaurus and Achelousaurus were separate in time, in 2010 Donald M. Henderson considered it possible that at least their descendants or ancestors were overlapping or sympatric and thus would have competed for food sources unless there had been niche partitioning.

facts.statement: During severe droughts, horned dinosaurs like Einiosaurus concentrated around oxbow lakes, leading to mass deaths and the formation of bone beds.
facts.quote: In such conditions, horned dinosaurs would have been dependent on oxbow lakes for a continuous supply of water and food – the main river channels tending to run dry earlier – and perished in them during severe droughts when the animals concentrated around the last watering holes, causing bone beds to form.

facts.statement: The generic name Einiosaurus combines the Blackfoot word for "buffalo" and the Greek word for "lizard."

facts.statement: Researchers believe that low-diversity bone beds of a single species represent herds that may have died in catastrophic events such as droughts or floods.
facts.quote: Se cree que los lechos de hueso de baja diversidad y de una sola especie representan rebaños que pueden haber muerto en eventos catastróficos, como durante una sequía o inundación.

facts.statement: Einiosaurus is evidence that it, like other centrosaurine ceratopsians, was a herd grazer with behavior similar to modern bison or nyu.
facts.quote: Esto es evidencia de que Einiosaurus , al igual que otros ceratopsianos centrosaurino como Pachyrhinosaurus y Centrosaurus , estaban pastoreando animales de comportamiento similar al bisonte moderno o al ñu.

facts.statement: A 2010 study by Julie Reizner concluded that Einiosaurus grew rapidly until its third or fifth year of life, after which growth slowed, likely at the onset of sexual maturity.

facts.statement: Like all ceratopsids, Einiosaurus had a complex dental battery capable of processing even the most resistant plants.

facts.statement: Contemporary dinosaurs included the basal ornithopod Orodromeus, hadrosaurids Hypacrosaurus, Maiasaura, and Prosaurolophus, ankylosaurians Edmontonia and Euoplocephalus, the tyrannosaurid Daspletosaurus which seems specialized in hunting ceratopsians, and smaller theropods Bambiraptor, Chirostenotes, Troodon, and the enantiornithine Avisaurus, as well as the ceratopsians Brachyceratops and Achelosaurus.
facts.quote: Los dinosaurios contemporáneos incluyen el ornitópodo basal Orodromeus, los hadrosáuridos Hypacrosaurus, Maiasaura, y Prosaurolophus, los anquilosaurianos Edmontonia y Euoplocephalus, el tiranosáurido Daspletosaurus que parece haber estado especialisado en cazar en ceratopsianos, así como terópodos más pequeños Bambiraptor, Chirostenotes, Troodon, y el enatiornies Avisaurus y los ceratópsidos Brachyceratops y Achelosaurus.

facts.statement: Einiosaurus lived in a climate that was seasonal, warm, and semi-arid.
facts.quote: Einiosaurus vivió en un clima que era estacional, cálido y semiárido.

facts.statement: Other fossils found with Einiosaurus material include freshwater bivalves and gastropods, implying these bones were deposited in a lake-dominated environment.
facts.quote: Otros fósiles encontraron con el material de Einiosaurus incluyen bivalvos y los gastrópodos de agua dulce, que implican que estos huesos fueron depositados en un ambiente dominado por un lago.
